The upper electrically-conductive portion (19t) is in contact with the lower electrically-conductive portion (3t) and the lateral surface and an upper surface of the lower portion (42) of the gate insulating layer (4) inside the contact hole.

The semiconductor device includes a thin-film transistor provided with an oxide semiconductor layer, together with a wire connecting portion. The wire connecting portion includes a lower conductive portion formed from the same conductive film as the gate electrode of the thin-film transistor.

An insulating layer is disposed over the lower conductive portion and includes a gate insulating layer, a protection layer, and an interlayer insulating layer. A contact hole is formed through the insulating layer so as to expose at least part of the lower conductive portion. At a lateral wall of the contact hole, the gate insulating layer includes a lower portion and an upper portion. When viewed in a direction normal to the substrate, the lateral surface of the lower portion protrudes beyond the lateral surface of the upper portion.

The wire connecting portion further includes an upper conductive portion that extends into the contact hole. Within the contact hole, the upper conductive portion is electrically connected to the exposed lower conductive portion and is also in contact with both the lateral surface and the upper surface of the protruding lower portion of the gate insulating layer.
outputs.L4:
A semiconductor device includes an oxide-semiconductor thin-film transistor and a wiring structure for electrically connecting conductive layers positioned at different levels. The transistor may include a gate electrode, a gate insulating layer covering the gate electrode, an oxide-semiconductor layer formed over the gate insulating layer, and source and drain electrodes electrically connected to the oxide-semiconductor layer. One of the electrodes or another conductive member constitutes a lower conductive portion that is covered by a multilayer insulating structure. The multilayer insulating structure includes the gate insulating layer and one or more additional insulating layers formed above it.

A contact hole is provided through the multilayer insulating structure to expose at least part of the lower conductive portion. An upper conductive portion is formed over the insulating structure and extends into the contact hole, thereby electrically connecting the upper conductive portion to the exposed lower conductive portion. Within or adjacent to the contact hole, a section of the gate insulating layer protrudes relative to the surrounding insulating layers. This protruding section has a side surface and a top surface, both of which are contacted by the upper conductive portion.

Because the upper conductive portion extends along multiple surfaces of the protruding gate-insulating section, it can be formed with improved coverage and mechanical stability in the contact region. The resulting geometry reduces the likelihood of discontinuities, inadequate step coverage, or separation of the upper conductive portion near the edge of the contact hole. It also provides a reliable electrical path between the upper and lower conductive portions. Accordingly, the semiconductor device achieves a robust contact structure and improved connection reliability while retaining the advantages of an oxide-semiconductor thin-film transistor.
outputs.L5:
### The Power of “The”

“The” is one of the smallest and most common words in the English language, yet it plays an essential role in communication. Known as the definite article, it points to a specific person, place, object, or idea. There is a clear difference between saying “a book” and “the book”: the first could mean any book, while the second refers to one that is already known or understood.

Because “the” appears so frequently, it is easy to overlook. However, this simple word helps create clarity and shared meaning. It quietly connects speakers and listeners by suggesting that both know what is being discussed.

In this way, “the” demonstrates that even the simplest words can carry significant power.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent-style abstract describing a semiconductor device with an oxide-semiconductor TFT and a wire connecting portion having a stepped gate-insulating-layer profile inside a contact hole.
counterfactuals.output: A semiconductor device includes a thin-film transistor comprising an oxide-semiconductor layer, a gate electrode, and a gate insulating layer interposed between the oxide-semiconductor layer and the gate electrode. The semiconductor device further includes a wiring layer electrically connected to the thin-film transistor through a contact hole formed in an insulating structure. Within the contact hole, the gate insulating layer has a stepped profile including portions positioned at different heights, and a conductive connection portion extends along the stepped profile to electrically couple the wiring layer to a conductive region of the thin-film transistor. The stepped profile reduces an abrupt change in surface level and improves coverage and continuity of the conductive connection portion. Accordingly, contact resistance and the likelihood of disconnection may be reduced while electrical reliability and manufacturing yield are improved.

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe the cross-sectional configuration of a TFT wire connecting portion, including the constituent insulating layers, the geometry of the contact-hole sidewall when viewed normal to the substrate, and the contact surfaces of the upper electrically conductive portion.
counterfactuals.output:
The TFT wire-connecting portion is formed as a laminated contact structure:

- A lower electrically conductive portion is provided on the substrate.
- It is covered by an insulating stack, typically including a lower inorganic insulating layer and an upper interlayer/planarizing insulating layer; an additional inorganic passivation layer may be included depending on the TFT structure.
- A contact hole penetrates the insulating layers and exposes the lower conductive portion.

Viewed in the direction normal to the substrate, the contact-hole sidewall is not defined by a sharp re-entrant corner. Adjacent sidewall portions are joined by a bent, rounded, or arcuate portion—i.e., the opening has a smoothly changing/obtuse contour that avoids an acute corner where the upper film could become thin or break.

An upper electrically conductive portion extends over the top insulating surface and down the contact-hole wall. At the bottom of the hole, it electrically contacts the exposed upper surface of the lower conductive portion and, where the hole exposes the conductor edge, also contacts a side surface of the lower conductive portion. This enlarged top-and-side contact improves connection reliability and suppresses wire disconnection.
